title: Geometric-point data for a zero-dimensional field base change
statement: Let k and k′ be algebraically closed fields and f:C→Spec k a separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most zero [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. In a cartesian square [def-pc-base-change] with lower map ι:Spec k′→Spec k and projection ι′:C′→C, C′→Spec k′ is again a curve of dimension at most zero. There is an equivalence b:|C′|≃|C| equal pointwise to ι′, and a family of geometric points s(c′):Spec k′→C′ [def-weil-geometric-point] with s(c′)(default)=c′. No sheaf occurs in this statement.

source.place: Degree-zero proof, point bijection and chosen geometric points; Stacks Tags 00KH, 00FV, 01JT.

proof.text: Recover the ring map k → k′ from ι by Spec.preimage and install its algebra structure. Apply the canonical zero-dimensional base-change point theorem. The isomorphism h.isoPullback identifies C′ with the canonical pullback; compose its underlying homeomorphism with the projection homeomorphism. Its underlying equivalence b agrees with ι′ by isoPullback_hom_fst. Invariance of topological Krull dimension under this isomorphism gives dimension at most zero.
Apply the three base-change stability properties to h: separatedness, local finite type, and quasi-compactness. Combine these with dimension at most zero, hence at most one, to construct IsCurve f′.

The canonical point theorem makes C discrete. The composed homeomorphism makes C′ discrete, so every singleton is closed. Apply the closed-point residue-field isomorphism over the algebraically closed field k′. Mathlib pointOfClosedPoint is Spec of that isomorphism followed by fromSpecResidueField; pointOfClosedPoint_apply verifies that this morphism sends default to c′. Taking this construction for every c′ gives the family s. The construction needs no nonempty hypothesis and therefore includes the empty scheme.

proof_origin.place: Degree-zero point description, transported explicitly with isoPullback; closed-point construction in Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.AlgClosed.Basic.
